summary: Iteration 13: tested the worker-first public pages, the Terms page and modal, the auth layout and hover readability. Backend: the new test_hyrz_iter13_terms_version.py passes 5/5. termsVersion '2026-10-19' or a missing version returns 400, termsAccepted=false returns 400, and '2026-11-06' gets through the terms check (a full worker sign-up returns 503 because there is no Resend key, which is expected). Frontend, passing: the home hero says 'Pick your own shifts. Get paid fast.'. home-find-shifts-button and public-pay-join-button open the worker register form, and home-employer-link and public-employer-cta open employer register. public-worker-benefits has 4 cards with visible yellow icons. The pay cards are readable. The carousel captions are worker-focused. The intro tabs read About us / How it works / For employers. The footer has Find shifts / Sign in / Hire staff / Terms & Conditions. There is no horizontal overflow at 1440. The Terms page opens from footer-terms-link: dark bar, Back returns home, a sticky contents list with Part A–D, 'In short' summaries and points like 14.1. It shows Version 2026-11-06 and has a print button. Clicking terms-contents-fees scrolls to that section and highlights it. At 390 the contents stack above the body. The sign-up modal scrolls (8095px of content in a 558px box). terms-agree-button switches the toggle on. 'Open the full page' and then Back keep the form data. A PAYE worker sign-up through the UI reaches 'Check your email' with the red couldn't-send notice. Role cards read 'I'm looking for work' / 'I'm hiring staff', and the form sits in the right half at 1440 and 1920. The left caption is now fully visible. Hover contrast is >= 4.5 on employer Dashboard, Checkouts (co-stat, Counter-offer, Message) and Favourites. Smoke tests pass: 5 PAYE badges for the worker, the fee-tier card on Invoices, the employer split inbox at 1440, and API login for worker, employer and admin. FAILURES: the Terms contents items turn white on light grey when hovered (about 1.1:1). Selected worker job tabs and admin sub-tabs show navy text on blue at rest. On mobile the employer strip runs past the right edge of the screen. The Terms page sticky bar covers section headings and the top of the contents list. There are 22 sections, not 23.

ui_bugs.issue: Hovered contents item text is #FFFFFF on #EDF2F7 (about 1.1:1, unreadable). RCA: styles.css:16103 has a global rule 'html body #root .app :where(a,button,[role=button],.clickable,.textbutton,.link-button):hover{color:#FFFFFF!important}' that overrides terms.css:9 (which has no !important). Fix: add to readability.css: html body #root:not(#x):not(#y) .terms-contents button:is(:hover,:focus-visible){color:#0F1B2D!important;-webkit-text-fill-color:#0F1B2D!important}. Also consider removing or narrowing that global white-on-hover rule, because it is the root cause of most hover readability bugs.

ui_bugs.component: Worker Jobs selected tab / admin selected sub-tabs (MESSAGES, ENQUIRIES) / employer 'Current workchats' pill
ui_bugs.issue: Text is navy on blue at rest (worker 'Available shifts' 2.83:1 on #1D5EC2; admin 3.85:1 on #2272EB). RCA: the rule '#root .app.worker button.selected, ... .app.admin button.selected ...' sets -webkit-text-fill-color:#0F1B2D, which wins over the color:#fff in readability.css lines 12 and 37 (fill colour beats color). Fix: add -webkit-text-fill-color:#fff!important to readability.css lines 12, 37 and 39.

The strip is width:100% (public.css: .auth-welcome>:is(.pub-section,.pub-employer-strip){width:100%}) plus a 16px side margin, so it measures x=16 to right=406 on a 390 viewport. It is clipped at the right edge and the right rounded corner and padding are lost. Fix: width:auto (or calc(100% - 32px)) for .pub-employer-strip.

The terms-page-bar is 63px tall and sticky, but .terms-section has scroll-margin-top:24px and .terms-contents has sticky top:24px. After clicking a contents item, the section heading (e.g. '14. Fees…') is half hidden under the bar, and when you scroll, the top of the contents list (the 'CONTENTS' label and Part A) slides under the bar. Fix: scroll-margin-top and the sticky top should be about 84px on the full page.

After scrolling section 18 (Your information) to the top, the highlighted contents item was 17 (Complaints and disputes). The IntersectionObserver callback uses es.find(isIntersecting), which takes the first entry in the batch rather than the top-most visible section. Minor.

issues: The home-employer-link 'Post a shift' and the terms-open-full-page 'Open the full page with contents' look like default browser buttons, with a 1px grey border, white background and Arial font, instead of plain text links. Add border:0; background:none; font:inherit.
In the terms modal, 'Agree to Terms & Conditions' looks like navy text on blue (same text-fill problem). Please verify its contrast.

The EXPLORE links (Find shifts, Sign in, Hire staff, Terms & Conditions, About us, How it works) and the 'Contact hyrz' button use the browser default font (Arial), while the OPPORTUNITIES column uses the brand font. This looks inconsistent.
The pagination dots are almost invisible: white and very light blue on the cream background.
The labels don't match: the nav says 'How we work', the tab says 'How it works' and the footer label says 'HOW WE WORK'.
Mobile 390: the nav labels 'About us' and 'How we work' wrap onto two lines and look cramped.
The 'Automated matching hours' line has no spacing between its parts ('Requested: 20–40 hrs/weekAccepted across Hyrz this week: 28.5 hrsRemaining available: 11.5 hrs').
The blue Chat button on a hovered (blue) card has almost no contrast against the card.
The review request says 23 numbered sections, but termsContent.js has 22. Add a section or correct the spec.
The employer dashboard says '1 shifts scheduled' (should pluralise correctly).

action_items: Fix the Terms contents hover colour (white on light grey) and ideally remove or narrow the global ':where(a,button,...):hover{color:#fff!important}' rule in styles.css:16103.
Add -webkit-text-fill-color:#fff to selected job tabs, admin selected tabs and selected pills, which currently show navy text on blue.
Fix the employer strip overflowing at 390 (width:100% plus margin).
Increase scroll-margin-top and the sticky top on the Terms page to clear the 63px bar.
Make the textbutton links (home-employer-link, terms-open-full-page) and the footer EXPLORE links use the brand font with no border.
Optional: fix the active-section tracking, the visibility of the carousel dots, and the inconsistent 'How it works'/'How we work' labels.
critical_code_review_comments: readability.css adds element-by-element overrides with :not(#x):not(#y) specificity hacks to fight a global !important white-on-hover rule. That is fragile: every new component (e.g. the Terms contents) hits the same bug. Remove the root rule instead.
Many rules set color but not -webkit-text-fill-color, while other rules set the fill colour. Standardise on one of them.
The Terms link button inside the signup-terms-row has no data-testid (only .inline-link).
The data-testid inbox-main-signout is no longer present in the employer split inbox, though a sign-out button is visible.
App.jsx is 1653 lines with very long lines. Split it into components.

seed_data_creation: Created TEST workers users.id 74 and 76 through pytest and id 75 through UI sign-up (PAYE). All were deleted by id, along with their audit_logs (actor_id), worker_pay_settings and worker_profiles rows. No test_iter13 users remain. No seed data was modified.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Login is rate-limited, so get tokens through the /api/auth/login API and inject them with localStorage.setItem('hyrz_token', token), then reload. Use /app/tests/hover_contrast.js (drop its first comment line) with el.evaluate to measure hover contrast; it honours -webkit-text-fill-color. The terms modal opens with '.signup-terms-row button.inline-link'. The register payChoice API needs contractAccepted:true and contractVersion 'hyrz-contractor-v1' or 'hyrz-paye-employment-v1'. To clean up users, delete audit_logs by actor_id, then worker_pay_settings, worker_profiles and users.
